q: A bank has clear data definitions and documented SOPs, yet different teams extract and aggregate the same data in different ways, producing inconsistent reports. In the bakery analogy, which component is weak?
explanation: L1 p.15: even with clear data definitions and business rules, you risk inconsistent results unless processes are adhered to. Formal processes and controls ensure data is extracted, transformed, aggregated and reported the right way.

q: In the bakery analogy, 'it doesn't matter how good the ingredients or recipe are, if the oven doesn't work the bread will not be good'. The oven represents:
explanation: L1 p.16: the oven = Technology Architecture. Differences in infrastructure can impact producing the right outputs in a timely fashion.

q: Which of the following belong to the 'Policies, Processes' (standard cookbook) component of the bakery analogy? Select all that apply.
options: Independent validations by internal and external audit
Reconciling data at each system hop
explanation: L1 p.14 lists common data models, golden sources and well-documented processes/assumptions under Policies, Processes. Independent validations sit under Monitoring Controls and Oversight (p.15); reconciliation at each system hop is a Technology Architecture note (p.16).

q: Which DCAM component covers 'structure, lines of authority, roles & responsibilities, escalation protocol, policy & standards, compliance, and routines'?
options: Data Management Program and Funding Model
explanation: L1 p.21: component 6, Data Governance.

q: 'Data operations, supply-chain management, cross-control function alignment, and collaborative technology architecture' describes which DCAM component?
explanation: L1 p.21: component 7, Data Control Environment.

q: Which pairing of framework and organisation is correct?
explanation: L1 p.20: DAMA International publishes DAMA-DMBOK2; the EDM Council publishes DCAM, 'the industry standard framework for data management'.

q: Which of these is NOT one of the 'Fundamentals' building blocks of good data governance?
explanation: L1 p.22: Fundamentals = Framework & Policies, DQ Identification & Assessment, Controls Environment. Monitoring & Reporting and Remediation are 'Ongoing Controls'; Independent Assessment is 'Continuous Improvement'.

q: Internal Audit performs an objective assessment of whether the requirements of the Data Management Policy are being met. Which line of defence is this?
explanation: L1 p.23: Internal Audit is the 3rd line, independent assurance and objective review of processes, controls and governance.

q: Which are responsibilities of the 2nd line of defence (Data Management Office)? Select all that apply.
options: Aligning resources to drive execution of data management activities
Day-to-day implementation and monitoring of data standards
Objective review of the effectiveness of internal controls
explanation: L1 p.23: the 2nd line is responsible for ensuring compliance, setting organisational priorities and aligning resources. Day-to-day implementation is the 1st line; objective review is Internal Audit (3rd line).

q: Under the data quality governance framework that mirrors the three lines of defence, who is accountable for the quality of their data?
explanation: L1 p.23: 'The Businesses are accountable for the quality of their data.' The DMO defines the programme structure; Internal Audit validates independently.

q: Under BCBS 239, 'risk systems should be capable of producing critical risk data rapidly during times of stress/crisis' falls under which principle?
explanation: L1 p.27: Principle 5 Timeliness. Adaptability (6) is about on-demand, ad hoc reporting incl. stress situations and supervisory queries; Frequency (10) is a risk-reporting principle.

q: Which of these are BCBS 239 Risk Data Aggregation principles? Select all that apply.
explanation: L1 p.27: Risk Data Aggregation = Accuracy & Integrity, Completeness, Timeliness, Adaptability. Comprehensiveness and Distribution are Risk Reporting principles (p.28).

q: BCBS 239 Accuracy & Integrity: controls on risk data should be as robust as those applied to:
explanation: L1 p.27: 'Controls on Risk data should be as robust as those applied to Finance data'; risk data should be reconciled with the bank's sources, incl. accounting data.

q: Which is NOT listed under BCBS 239 Principle 2 (Data architecture & IT infrastructure)?
options: Risk data reconciled with the bank's sources, including accounting data
Integrated data taxonomies and architecture across the bank
Data ownership roles and responsibilities clearly defined
explanation: L1 p.27: reconciliation with accounting data is under Principle 3, Accuracy & Integrity. The other three are Principle 2.

q: How did the CBIRC perform its checks on banks?
options: Using the EAST inspection analysis system (Examination & Analysis System Technology)
By requiring each bank to self-assess against BCBS 239
Through the EDM Council's DCAM benchmarking
Through banks' own Internal Audit reports
explanation: L1 p.26: CBIRC used EAST, with modules incl. standardised data collection/extraction models, on-site inspection management, data modelling tools and data model release.

q: Which are among the 7 parts of the CBIRC data governance guidelines? Select all that apply.
explanation: L1 p.25: General, Data Governance, Data Management, Data Quality & Controls, Data Monetisation, Supervision & Management, Supplementary. Risk Reporting is a BCBS 239 grouping; Analytics Management is a DCAM component.

q: According to the slide on CBIRC findings, banks were fined in April mainly for:
options: Under-reporting or inaccurate reporting (e.g. client information, regulatory reports)
Failing to appoint a Chief Data Officer
Moving customer data to the cloud without approval
explanation: L1 p.26: 8 banks were fined CNY17.7m for under-reporting or inaccurate reporting of client information, regulatory reports, interbank and trade finance transactions, etc.

q: A bank adds a spending-insights analytics feature to its existing credit card app to make the card more attractive to customers. Under the MIT framework this is:
explanation: L2 p.16: Wrapping delivers value indirectly by bundling core products with analytics features and experiences, increasing the product value proposition.

q: A company uses its operational data to streamline its processes and reduce overhead costs. Under the MIT framework this is:
explanation: L2 p.16: Improving delivers value indirectly by improving processes and work tasks with data, reducing COGS or overheads.

q: Which MIT monetisation method involves the DIRECT conversion of data or information solutions into revenue?
explanation: L2 p.16: Selling = direct conversion into revenue. Improving and Wrapping deliver value indirectly.

q: A data provider can reasonably quantify the cost savings a consumer would gain from using its dataset. Which valuation approach fits best?
explanation: L2 p.20: the Income approach applies if net cash flow benefits can be reasonably quantified; one form is 'reduced cost' (cost savings from using the data).

q: 'Value based on the estimated cost of replicating the UTILITY of the data' is:
explanation: L2 p.19: replacement cost = cost of replicating the utility of data; reproduction cost = cost of reproducing a replica of the data.

q: Which valuation approach asks 'What is the minimum value to cover costs and generate margin?'
explanation: L2 p.19: Cost approach, used if the data can be reproduced or replaced.

q: Which are forms of the Market approach to data valuation? Select all that apply.
explanation: L2 p.18: Market approach = actively traded market or market transactions. Reproduction cost is Cost approach (p.19); incremental revenue and reduced cost are Income approach (p.20).

q: 'The Data Management Strategy must be a ________ that is visibly endorsed by executive management, supported and prioritised by stakeholders and enabled by technology.'
explanation: L2 p.13: a living artifact, which should be routinely revisited and must evolve as priorities change.

q: Which is NOT a characteristic of a data strategy per the slides?
options: It is fixed once approved, to give the organisation certainty
It aligns with business goals and objectives
It is actionable, measurable and relevant
It identifies key support, resources and constraints
explanation: L2 p.10 and p.13: a strategy is a living document that should be routinely revisited and must evolve as priorities change.

q: Which are core components of a data strategy document? Select all that apply.
explanation: L2 p.12 lists principles, stakeholder analysis, objectives/scope, target state, current state gap analysis, data control approach, governance framework, DQ approach, IT and cross-functional collaboration, resource plan, funding approach, business case, execution roadmap, measurement approach.

q: 'Driving brand loyalty/reputation and developing proprietary knowledge, systems & processes' is which financial value from improved data?
explanation: L2 p.4: improving social capital, which can be converted into economic capital.

q: In the process to prepare data for sale (data provider's perspective), which step comes immediately after 'Assess potential for sharing'?
explanation: L2 p.17: Stock-take → Assess data → Assess potential for sharing → Select valuation approach → Value the data → Share the data.

q: Per Lecture 2, which function plays an integral role in selecting the appropriate valuation approach to assess the value of data?
explanation: L2 p.18: 'Finance would play an integral role in helping to select the appropriate VALUATION APPROACH.'

q: 'Central + selective localised capability distribution, with centralised control' describes which data management structure?
explanation: L3 p.10: Federated (hub and spoke). Decentralised has no central control; centralised is a single point of control at enterprise level.

q: Each business unit of a conglomerate runs its own data function with complete autonomy and no central control. Reports show duplicated efforts and inconsistent quality across BUs. Which structure is this?
explanation: L3 p.10: decentralised = complete BU autonomy, no central control; cons include disjointed, duplicated efforts and inconsistent quality across BUs.

q: 'Faster decision making; greater data consistency across BUs' are listed pros of which structure?
explanation: L3 p.10: centralised pros are faster decision making, greater data consistency across BUs, better efficiency/minimal duplication. Decentralised offers 'quick decision making at BU level'; federated has slower decision making.

q: Which are listed PROS of the federated (hub and spoke) model? Select all that apply.
options: Easy to cross-pollinate capacity, skills and best practices
Quick decision making at BU level
explanation: L3 p.10. 'Quick decision making at BU level' is a decentralised pro; 'faster decision making' is a centralised pro. Federated's con is slower decision making.

q: Per the pros and cons analysis, central structures suit ______ organisations and federated structures suit ______ organisations.
explanation: L3 p.8: central is for less mature organisations (control, structure, oversight); federated is for more mature data organisations (alignment and ownership to BUs).

q: Per the slides, whether the CDO should report to the CEO, CRO or CFO depends on:
options: The reason for establishing the CDO position
The size of the bank's balance sheet
The number of critical data elements
Whether the bank is a G-SIB
explanation: L3 p.8: depends on the reason for establishing the CDO: regulatory compliance vs business innovation vs data quality risks.

q: A bank faces a regulatory push on AML/KYC and recent regulatory submission errors. Per the slides, what should the CDO role focus on?
options: Purely on data governance for a start
Data analytics and innovation, as a CDAO
Reporting to the CTO to fix systems
Handing governance to the Data Governance Committee
explanation: L3 p.8: analytics adds depth, but if organisations have inherent data issues (e.g. AML/KYC push, regulatory submission errors, new compliance rules) it might be good to focus purely on data governance for a start.

q: Which body is 'the principal senior management body that supports and is accountable to the BoD on the effectiveness of the Group's data management policies and controls'?
explanation: L3 p.13: the DGC. It comprises senior management from key business areas, Risk, Finance and Group T&O.

q: Which are roles of the Board of Directors in the typical DG structure? Select all that apply.
options: Provide strategic direction and define strategic initiatives
Approve data governance policies and changes proposed by the DGC
Act as the forum for deliberation and issue escalation on data matters
Enforce data standards day to day
explanation: L3 p.12: Board provides strategic direction, funding, direction on KPIs/metrics, and approves DG policies. The forum for deliberation and escalation is the DGC (p.13).

q: In the typical data governance structure, at which level do Data Owners, Business Data Stewards, System Owners and Technical Data Stewards sit?
explanation: L3 p.11: Strategic = Board; Executive = DGC; Management = CDO & DMO; Execution = owners and stewards.

q: The CDO's responsibilities are broadly classified into three areas. Which is NOT one of them?
explanation: L3 p.14: Data Governance, Data Architecture & Tools and Data Quality. Internal Audit is the independent 3rd line (L1 p.23).

q: Per the EDM Council benchmark cited in Lecture 3, what gave the finance industry a 'head start' in developing data management programmes?
explanation: L3 p.3: the 2008 Financial Crisis.

q: Who typically heads the Data Governance Committee?
options: The CDO's reporting head, or the CDO
explanation: L3 p.13: 'Head of DGC is typically the reporting head of the CDO or the CDO himself.'

q: Who has a clear understanding of the data they own, sets the standards for the data, and is ACCOUNTABLE for data quality?
explanation: L4 p.5: Data Owner. Business data stewards enforce standards and are RESPONSIBLE for DQ.

q: Department representatives who support data owners, ENFORCE standards for data and are RESPONSIBLE for data quality are:
explanation: L4 p.5: Business Data Stewards. Owners set standards and are accountable.

q: Finance receives transaction data from Operations, prepares regulatory reports, and also passes aggregated figures to the Risk team. What is Finance's stakeholder role?
options: Both a Data Consumer and a Data Provider
The Data Owner of the Operations data
explanation: L4 p.5: if a Data Consumer provides data to downstream users, they are also Data Providers.

q: Customer address is copied from the CRM system into the data warehouse without any transformation. What happens to data ownership?
options: No change; no new data element has been created
Ownership transfers to the data warehouse team
Ownership becomes shared between CRM and warehouse teams
explanation: L4 p.6: if a data element is transferred without any transformation, there is no change in Data Ownership.

q: The Risk team defines the criteria to derive a new 'high-risk customer' flag from several existing fields; IT builds the job. Who becomes the Data Owner of the new flag?
options: The Risk team, as the stakeholder who defines the transformation criteria
The owners of the source fields
The IT team that runs the transformation job
explanation: L4 p.6: if a new data element is created by transformation, the Data Stakeholder who defines the transformation criteria becomes the new Data Owner.

q: If Data Owners still cannot be determined using proximity and authority, ownership is:
options: Decided by a vote of the Data Governance Committee
explanation: L4 p.6: assignment by CDO.

q: Which are impacts of a data element being identified as a CDE? Select all that apply.
options: Its standard definition is agreed and documented
It is exempted from routine DQ monitoring
It must be reported to the regulator every month
explanation: L4 p.7: standard definition agreed, appears in data-flow docs, full lineage documented, subject to heightened controls, quality monitoring and governance.

q: Have regulators provided guidance on how CDEs should be identified?
options: No; they expect banks to explain their process and rationale for prioritising data
Yes; BCBS 239 lists the CDEs every bank must use
Yes; MAS prescribes the CDE criteria
No; CDE identification is optional for banks
explanation: L4 p.7: regulators have not provided guidance but expect banks to explain their process; industry collaborated with the EDMC on principles.

q: Customer profiles require access limitations and have regulatory privacy considerations. Which CDE criterion makes them more critical?
options: Data Attribute Usage for Regulatory Purposes
explanation: L4 p.8: criterion 2, Information Security / Privacy; example: customer profiles.

q: Capital charge, leverage ratio and earnings per share would most likely be CDEs under which criterion?
explanation: L4 p.9: criterion 6, Enterprise Performance (data used for key performance measurements).

q: 'Number of customer complaints' and 'number of critical system downtime by month' are examples for which CDE criterion?
explanation: L4 p.9: criterion 7, Operational Risk (data that if incorrect could cause operational risk losses).

q: In the Fine Revenue worked example, which CDE criteria were marked for 'No of people fined'? Select all that apply.
explanation: L4 p.12: 'No of people fined' is marked 1, 3, 5 (Regulatory, Reporting Level, Financial Impact). 'Penalty per fine' is 1, 4, 5.

q: Which data culture building blocks fall under 'Tone at the top'? Select all that apply.
explanation: L4 p.15: Tone at the top = KPIs & rewards, corporate values, senior communications, long-term sustainability. Capability building is 'Embedding into operations'; upgrading tools is 'Enabled by'.

q: 'A social norm of using data to drive strategy, decisions and innovation' defines:
explanation: L4 p.4: data culture.

q: 'Manage risks through preventing, detecting, or correcting activities and can be automated or procedural' defines:
explanation: L4 p.4: data controls.

q: 'Those who use, affect, or are affected by data' are:
explanation: L4 p.4: data stakeholders.

q: 'A centralised repository of metadata including tables, fields, databases, data type, size, explanation, source, application, owners, default values' is a:
explanation: L5 p.12: data dictionary.

q: 'A collection of all terms that define your data's key characteristics, organised in a way that is easy to search, giving context and helping organise knowledge' is a:
explanation: L5 p.12: business glossary.

q: 'Understanding, recording and visualising data as it flows from sources to consumption, including all transformations: how it was transformed, what changed, and why' is:
explanation: L5 p.12: data lineage. A data flow diagram shows how information flows through a process or system (inputs, outputs, stores, subprocesses).

q: A project team implementing a new system needs to confirm the golden source of each data element and approvals for authorised use. Which documentation is most useful?
explanation: L5 p.19: the data dictionary is used especially during system implementation for golden sources of data and approvals for authorised use.

q: Which types of data documentation are maintained by Technology and business process owners? Select all that apply.
explanation: L5 p.19: DFD and lineage are maintained by Technology and business process owners; glossary and dictionary by the DMO with data owners.

q: Which are classified as BUSINESS documentation? Select all that apply.
explanation: L5 p.10: business documentation = business glossary and data flow diagram; technical = data dictionary and data lineage.

q: Which policy contains a section on DQ dimensions, rules and thresholds?
explanation: L5 p.8: Data Quality Controls (DQ dimensions, rules, thresholds) is a core component of the Data Quality Policy.

q: 'Scope inclusions and exclusions' and 'Stages of data sharing' are core components of which policy?
explanation: L5 p.9: Data Sharing Policy.

q: Which is NOT a core component of the Data Management Policy?
options: Data Architecture: golden source, metadata, reference data, master data
explanation: L5 p.7 vs p.9: 'Stages of data sharing' belongs to the Data Sharing Policy.

q: In an employee table, which of the following is METADATA?
options: The column name 'employee_id' and its data type 'int'
The value 44 in the employee_id column
Department number 1 recorded for a row
explanation: L5 p.11: the column headers (and their definitions in the data dictionary) are metadata, 'data about the data'; the rows are data.

q: In the typical DG framework, which sit under Information Lifecycle Management? Select all that apply.
explanation: L5 p.5: ILM = data acquisition, data security, data usage and access, EUC management, data retention, data sharing. Golden sources are under Data Architecture; DQ monitoring under Data Quality.

q: Which documentation is described as providing an end-to-end understanding of data flow to identify control gaps and streamlining opportunities?
explanation: L5 p.19: data flow diagram. Lineage gives a deep understanding of transformation through the life cycle. Both are used for forensic root-cause investigation.

q: In the sample data dictionary, what does the 'Golden Source' field indicate?
options: The authoritative source for the data element
The data owner of the element
The system with the most users
The downstream report that uses the element
explanation: L5 p.14: 'Indicate the authoritative source for the data element' (e.g. EDW (Core)).

q: In the sample data dictionary, a Timeliness value of 'T+1' means:
options: The data element is published in the system 1 day after the transaction date
The data is refreshed every hour
Errors must be fixed within 1 business day
explanation: L5 p.14: format T+X, where X is the age in days between the transaction date and the day the data element is published.

q: A feed contains invalid ISO currency codes. Which DQ dimension is breached?
explanation: L6 p.7: Conformity = alignment of content with required standards; examples include invalid ISO currency codes.

q: One system stores dates in US format and another in European format for the same records. Which DQ dimension is breached?
explanation: L6 p.8: Consistency = values, format and definitions in one population agree with those in another; example: US vs European date formats. (Conformity's example is 'inconsistent date formats' against a required standard.)

q: Bond records have a null maturity date. Which DQ dimension is breached?
explanation: L6 p.7: Completeness = existence of required data attributes; example: null maturity date.

q: The same customer appears under two different customer IDs. Which DQ dimension is breached?
explanation: L6 p.8: Uniqueness = singularity of records and attributes; example: customer with different Cus IDs.

q: A revised credit rating was not updated in the system on the day it was issued. Which DQ dimension is breached?
explanation: L6 p.8 lists 'revised credit rating not updated on day it was issued' as a Timeliness example.

q: Which DQ dimension is defined as 'breadth and availability of data'?
explanation: L6 p.8: Coverage.

q: Which is NOT one of the seven EDM Council DQ dimensions taught in Lecture 6?
explanation: L6 pp.7-8: Accuracy, Completeness, Conformity, Consistency, Coverage, Timeliness, Uniqueness.

q: Which of these are given as examples of ACCURACY issues in Lecture 6? Select all that apply.
options: Records are wrong at specified time
Wrong level of precision (e.g. decimal places)
explanation: L6 p.7: accuracy examples are records wrong at specified time, records not refreshed/updated and wrong precision. Invalid ISO codes = conformity; null maturity date = completeness.

q: The system only accepts Customer IDs of 2 alphabets + 6 digits. This control addresses which dimension?
explanation: L6 p.10: system restriction on permitted values/formats is the Conformity control example.

q: Two systems holding the same Customer ID are reconciled, with the golden source as the reliable source of truth. This control addresses which dimension?
explanation: L6 p.11: reconciliation of two systems is the Consistency control example.

q: A maker-checker ensures a Customer ID is assigned to every customer, making it a compulsory system field. This control addresses which dimension?
explanation: L6 p.10: the Completeness control example.

q: Inadequate UAT scenarios and upstream system enhancements not in sync with downstream applications fall under which root cause category?
explanation: L6 p.6: category 3, Program logic / Data transformation logic.

q: Batch scheduling errors and code deployment errors fall under which root cause category?
explanation: L6 p.6: category 4, Data operational errors (also configuration errors and operational adjustments not communicated downstream).

q: Which are listed under 'Data errors from external parties'? Select all that apply.
explanation: L6 p.6. Transposition errors are EUC errors; code deployment errors are data operational errors.

q: Which of these are End User Computing (EUC) errors per Lecture 6? Select all that apply.
explanation: L6 p.6: EUC errors = incorrect template or data source, typographical errors, transposition errors. Batch scheduling = data operational; inadequate UAT = program/transformation logic.

q: An analyst's Excel reporting template points at last month's data source, so the month-end report is wrong. Which root cause category?
explanation: L6 p.6: EUC errors include incorrect template or data source.

q: Why do the slides describe the traditional approach to data quality as difficult?
options: It is long and arduous; building rules, measuring, solving root causes and remediating takes time, and the delay is costly
It requires AI/ML expertise most banks lack
Regulators no longer accept rules-based checks
It cannot measure data quality at all

q: 'Specific rules and formula; high human intervention; reactive on an after-event basis' describes which approach?
explanation: L6 p.15: rules-based.

q: 'Create DQ flags; impute missing values; real-time prediction and model improvement' describes which AI/ML approach?
explanation: L6 p.15: predictive modelling.

q: 'A measure of the degree to which the collected data is fit for the intended purpose' defines:
explanation: L4 p.4; the DQ objective on L6 p.4 is trusted, fit-for-purpose data.

q: A CDE's DQ result is 94%. How is it interpreted?
explanation: L7 p.15: 95%+ very good; 92.5%-95% good; <92.5% fair.

q: A CDE's DQ result is 92%. How is it interpreted?
explanation: L7 p.15: less than 92.5% is 'Fair'. There is no 'Poor' band on the slide.

q: 2,000 records were assessed and 80 failed the DQ rules applied. Using the slide formula, what is the DQ result and interpretation?
explanation: L7 p.15: (2,000 − 80) / 2,000 × 100% = 96%, which is in the '95% and up' band (Very good).

q: Which statements about the DQ result are correct per the slides? Select all that apply.
options: It reflects the number of data which violated the rules in the entire population
False positives have been removed from the population
It represents the actual deviation of the data (e.g. accuracy)
False positives are counted as failures
explanation: L7 p.15: it counts violations in the entire population, false positives removed, and it does NOT represent the actual deviation of the data.

q: In the approach to DQ rules design, what is Step 2?
options: Classify the CDE to the right data type
Understand the CDE and conduct data profiling
Design rules for each DQ dimension
explanation: L7 p.4: Step 1 profiling, Step 2 data type classification, Step 3 DQ dimensions.

q: How do the slides describe data profiling?
options: The first but most critical step to reviewing the 'state of affairs' of the data
Optional if the CDE is already in the data dictionary
A check used only for unique identifiers

q: Profiling of 1,000 employee records finds 2 different employee names with the same NRIC number. What did the slide conclude?
options: Uniqueness issue: incorporate as a uniqueness rule
Conformity issue: incorporate as a conformity rule
Completeness issue: incorporate as a completeness rule
HR Manager to look into it; keep as a generic rule

q: Profiling finds 10 employees with employment start date 1/1/1900. What did the slide conclude?
options: These employees left more than 5 years ago; fine-tune the rule for active employees only

q: Currency code is classified as which data type for DQ rule design?
explanation: L7 p.7: values taken from an external reference (e.g. ISO); examples: country of operations, currency code, issuer rating.

q: Which are given as examples of 'Unique identifiers'? Select all that apply.
explanation: L7 p.7: unique identifier examples are customer name, customer account number, passport number/NRIC. Cost centre is an internal reference table; issuer rating is an external reference value.

q: An accuracy rule checks that data can be verified to an external source such as Moody's/S&P/Fitch ratings or the ACRA Business File. This rule type is:
explanation: L7 p.8: verifiability. Validity checks e.g. that the customer exists and is backed by documentation.

q: The uniqueness rule (checking no duplicate exists) is best suited to which data type?
Which is NOT a completeness rule type in Lecture 7?
options: Checking that the end date is always later than the start date
Checking that the field is not null
Checking that the field is not filled with 'N/A', 'NIL' or default values
Checking that the total number of records in the table is complete
explanation: L7 p.9 vs p.12: end date later than start date is listed under the timeliness rules (marked 'for accuracy').

q: A rule checks that every loan record is linked to an existing customer. Per Lecture 7, this is a rule for which dimension?
explanation: L7 p.11: 'checking whether logical relationships are present (e.g., loan records should be linked to an existing customer)' is a consistency rule.

q: What is the correct order of the process for measuring data quality?
Per the slides, DQ thresholds are agreed on what basis?
options: Acceptable quality for the business user, based on risk tolerance and regulatory requirements
A fixed 95% set by regulators for all data
Whatever the DQ tool vendor recommends
explanation: L7 p.14; the L9 recap adds that thresholds are set by users as the % of records that minimally need to be right.

q: An Operational Risk Controls Attestation on data quality is done in Excel on an annual/bi-annual basis. This is an example of:
explanation: L7 p.16: manual (Excel) vs automated via tools such as Informatica, IBM, Talend (monthly/quarterly DQ team testing).

q: Which describe the Remediation step of DQ measurement? Select all that apply.
options: Perform one-time corrections to correct the errors
Enhance processes/systems to improve controls strategically
Agree acceptable quality based on risk tolerance
Highlight issues, root causes, owners and timelines
explanation: L7 p.14: remediation = one-time corrections + strategic enhancements. Agreeing acceptable quality is Thresholds; highlighting issues is Dashboard.

q: A rule flags a term loan completed in 2009 that still shows as active in 2019. Which rule type is this?
options: Timeliness: checking against the history of the record

q: 'A bridge between the requirements for data of the business process and the physical execution of that data in technology infrastructure' defines:
'How data, tools and platforms operate in collaboration to satisfy business requirements, enabling cost control, scalability and elasticity' defines:
'Classification of data into hierarchical groups to create structure, standardise terminology, and popularise a dataset' is:
Which 'restricts the set of valid values for each data field'?
explanation: L8 p.8 (and p.9 definition of reference data).

q: Which are examples of PUBLIC reference data? Select all that apply.
explanation: L8 p.9: public = country codes, currency codes, external risk rating categories, legal entity identifiers. Chart of accounts and product codes are private.

q: Source 1 records a customer's country as 'Singapore'; Source 2 records 'SG'. Both are looked up in a table and updated to 'SGP'. This illustrates:
options: Reference data in practice: updating records to enterprise standards

q: In the 'bricks' illustration of data architecture, which are the 'sorted bricks'?
options: Data domain, data taxonomy, reference data
Data flow diagram, data lineage, data inventory
explanation: L8 p.6: individual bricks = CDEs, dictionary; sorted = domain, taxonomy, reference data; aggregated = DFD, lineage, inventory; output = data model.

q: Which data domain 'contains enterprise, geographic location, entity set up, BU and cost centre set ups'?
In the metadata management tool, which capabilities fall under 'Trusting the data'? Select all that apply.
explanation: L8 p.14: Trusting = auditability, DQ rules, analytics dashboard, exception management, discovery & profiling. Pipelines = Using the data; lineage = Understanding the data.

q: 'Regulators write machine-readable code as a set of reporting instructions instead of natural language' describes:
'A global, platform-independent, machine-readable and unambiguous data standard that enables understanding of financial terminology' is:
In the ASEAN Data Management Framework, the impact/risk assessment uses which parameters?
explanation: L9 p.12: component 4 assesses impact if confidentiality (C), integrity (I) or availability (A) is compromised.

q: 'Classification must be automated for all data at point of creation or ingestion and must be always on' belongs to which CDMC area?
explanation: L9 p.11: control 6, under 2.0 Cataloguing & Classification.

q: 'The less restricted the use of the shared data is, the higher its value' describes which data value driver?
'Bias in data collection (selection, exclusion, reporting, detection bias) leading to over or under representation' is which data characteristic influencing AI?
Which are listed as Finance's role in the data lifecycle? Select all that apply.
options: Valuation of data as an asset
Independent validation / assurance over data quality and processes
Impact analysis for data quality issues
explanation: L9 p.17: robust controls & governance, valuation of data as an asset, monitoring DQ, independent validation/assurance, impact analysis for DQ issues.

q: Which is NOT an objective of the MAS FEAT Principles?
options: Prescribing the DQ thresholds firms must meet for AI models
Providing foundational principles for firms using AIDA in decision-making
Assisting firms to operationalise governance of AIDA use
Promoting public confidence and trust in the use of AIDA
explanation: L9 p.10 lists the three objectives; no DQ thresholds are prescribed.

q: Under the ASEAN Model Contractual Clauses, who must notify the relevant authorities and the Data Exporter of a data breach?
explanation: L9 p.13: the Data Importer shall notify without undue delay or within an agreed time.
